title: Focus the SBA only on programs Congress has authorized
proposal: The chapter calls for a smaller, more focused Small Business Administration that concentrates on programs Congress has authorized, rather than expanding into new areas.
quote: A tighter, more focused SBA that concentrates on congressionally authorized programs.

title: Make SBA staff report regularly and act on watchdog advice
proposal: The chapter says the SBA Administrator and staff should report regularly to Congress, answer lawmakers' requests on time, and carry out or respond to Inspector General and GAO recommendations.
quote: An accountable SBA Administrator and staff who report regularly to Congress, respond on a timely basis to requests from individual Members of Congress

title: Account for and recover COVID-19 relief fraud (PPP and EIDL)
proposal: The chapter calls for a full accounting of fraud in COVID-19 relief programs like PPP and EIDL. People who were not eligible for forgiveness or lied on applications would have to repay or be referred to law enforcement.
quote: A full accounting of and an end to waste, fraud, and abuse in all COVID-19 relief programs, including the PPP and EIDL programs

title: End SBA direct lending
proposal: The chapter calls for the SBA to stop making loans directly to borrowers and to state clearly that no new direct lending programs will be created at the SBA.
quote: An end to SBA direct lending.

title: Run SBA programs first-come, first-served for all small businesses
proposal: The chapter says SBA outreach should reach all eligible small businesses, and programs should not duplicate one another and should be offered on a first-come, first-served basis.
quote: Programs would be nonduplicative and implemented on a first-come, first-served basis.

title: Have SBA Advocacy measure the total cost of federal regulation
proposal: The chapter says the SBA Office of Advocacy should get a renewed mandate and more resources to fight overregulation, including research measuring the total cost federal rules place on small businesses.
quote: a research agenda that includes measuring the total cost that federal regulation imposes on small businesses.

title: Require SBA performance metrics and anti-fraud safeguards
proposal: The chapter says the SBA should be required to adopt performance measures and internal procedures to protect taxpayer money and program integrity.
quote: Require performance metrics and internal procedures to safeguard taxpayer dollars and program integrity.

title: Carry out watchdog recommendations within 90 days
proposal: The chapter says SBA management should address open Inspector General and GAO recommendations within a set time, ideally within 90 days of each recommendation.
quote: require that SBA management implement or address outstanding and ongoing OIG and GAO recommendations within a specified time frame

title: Give SBA Advocacy an early look at proposed rules
proposal: The chapter proposes changing the Regulatory Flexibility Act so agencies must send proposed rules and small-business impact analyses to the Office of Advocacy at least 60 days before publishing them, and respond to its comments.
quote: Amend the RFA so that all agencies are required to provide a copy of any proposed rule (other than bona fide emergency rules)

title: Count indirect costs in small-business rule analysis
proposal: The chapter says the economic analysis agencies do under the Regulatory Flexibility Act should include indirect costs as well as direct costs.
quote: RFA economic analysis should be expanded to include indirect costs along with direct costs.

title: Exempt small businesses from new rules unless Advocacy signs off
proposal: The chapter says Congress should presume small businesses are exempt from new agency rules, and let rules apply to them only if the Office of Advocacy signs off under set criteria. It also says agencies should be required to seek Advocacy's input.
quote: Congress should presumptively exempt small businesses from new agency rules to force agencies to seek Advocacy's input

title: Raise the SBA Office of Advocacy budget by at least 50%
proposal: The chapter recommends increasing the Office of Advocacy's budget by at least 50 percent ($4.6 million) so it can hire about 25 more attorneys, economists, and scientists.
quote: Increase the Office of Advocacy's budget by at least 50 percent ($4.6 million).

title: Direct agencies to comply with the Regulatory Flexibility Act
proposal: The chapter says the President should explicitly direct agencies to follow the Regulatory Flexibility Act, and the Office of Advocacy should hold regional roundtables and an online platform to hear from small businesses.
quote: Explicitly direct federal agencies to comply with the RFA.

title: Use private-sector help to close out COVID loan programs
proposal: The chapter says the next Administration should consider bringing in private-sector help to wrap up COVID-19 loan programs, pursue fraud, and require ineligible PPP recipients to repay.
quote: Consider bringing in private-sector support and expertise to close out these programs.

title: Review and possibly reverse PPP loan forgiveness for Planned Parenthood
proposal: The chapter says the SBA should find out whether it can reverse forgiveness of PPP loans to Planned Parenthood affiliates; if so, it should reverse them, investigate, and refer any knowing misrepresentation to the Justice Department.
quote: If it does have that authority, the SBA should reverse the forgiveness decisions for the subject loans

title: Study moving disaster loans out of the SBA
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should work with Congress to decide whether another agency should run disaster loans instead of the SBA, and explore private-sector ways to administer them.
quote: Work with Congress to assess the extent to which disaster loans should be offered by another agency rather than the SBA

title: Tell Congress SBA won't enforce religious exclusion rules
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should notify Congress that it will not enforce SBA rules that bar certain religious organizations from some loan programs, calling those rules unconstitutional.
quote: Notify Congress under 28 U.S. Code § 530D that it will not enforce these unconstitutional regulations.

title: Remove SBA Form 1971 (religious eligibility worksheet)
proposal: The chapter says the SBA should take down Form 1971, the worksheet it uses to decide whether religious entities may get loans.
quote: Take down SBA Form 1971.

title: Remove religious exclusions from SBA loan rules
proposal: The chapter says the SBA should finalize the Trump Administration's proposed rule, or issue a new one, to remove regulations that make some religious entities ineligible for SBA loans.
quote: Finalize the Trump Administration's proposed rule or publish its own updated proposed rule to remove the unconstitutional regulations.

title: Continue the SBIR and STTR research grant programs
proposal: The chapter says the Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer programs, which direct some federal research money to small firms, should continue.
quote: Continue the SBIR and SBTT programs as they successfully fund the next wave of technological innovation to compete with Big Tech.

title: Increase the research money agencies must set aside for SBIR
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should urge Congress to raise the share of other agencies' research budgets that must go to the SBIR small-business program.
quote: Urge Congress to expand the amount that other agencies are required to set aside from their general R&D budgets for the SBIR program.

title: Require SBIR funds to be spent on U.S. capital investment
proposal: The chapter calls for stricter rules requiring that SBIR program money be spent on capital investments inside the United States.
quote: Ensure the enactment of stricter rules requiring that SBIR funds must be expended on capital investments in the United States.

title: Create larger SBA 7(a) loans for manufacturing facilities
proposal: The chapter says Congress should create a category of SBA 7(a) loans with a higher maximum amount for building manufacturing facilities and upgrading equipment. It cites a past bill that would have raised the cap to $50 million.
quote: Ask Congress to make available a category of Section 7(a) loans with a larger available principal that is used to finance manufacturing facility construction

title: Refocus the SBIC program on small manufacturers, not just tech
proposal: The chapter says the Small Business Investment Company program should focus on small businesses broadly rather than mainly tech startups, and Congress should make its financing better suited to manufacturers, such as longer-term loans.
quote: Reform the Small Business Investment Company (SBIC) program to refocus its support on small businesses rather than technology startups only.

title: Create a "medium-sized business" classification
proposal: The chapter says Congress should create a medium-sized business category, with eligibility limited to capital-access programs where credit is not available elsewhere.
quote: Encourage Congress to create a "medium-sized business" classification with its eligibility for programs confined to access to capital programs

title: Support the IMPROVE the SBA Act
proposal: The chapter says the new Administration can support the IMPROVE the SBA Act, which it says would strengthen accountability, transparency, and oversight of the SBA.
quote: The IMPROVE the SBA Act68 would strengthen accountability, transparency, and oversight of the SBA

title: Support the Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act
proposal: The chapter supports a bill that would require agencies to do more detailed small-business economic analysis for rules and would waive fines for some first-time paperwork violations.
quote: would require federal agencies to perform more thorough RFA economic analysis and provide a rationale for proposed regulations.

title: Extend small-business review panels to all federal agencies
proposal: The chapter says the SBREFA panel process, which lets small businesses give input on agency rules before they are proposed, should apply to all federal agencies.
quote: SBREFA panel requirements should be extended to all federal agencies.

title: Bar project labor agreements in federal contracting
proposal: The chapter supports the Fair and Open Competition Act, which would stop the federal government from using project labor agreements on construction contracts, as required by President Biden's Executive Order 14063.
quote: The Fair and Open Competition Act71 would disallow the use of project labor agreements (PLAs) in federal contracting

title: Support the JOBS Act 4.0 to update SEC capital rules
proposal: The chapter supports the JOBS Act 4.0, which it says would update Securities and Exchange Commission rules to make it easier for businesses to raise money.
quote: would advance regulatory improvements and modernization of various Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) rules to enhance capital formation and access.

title: Pick an SBA chief with finance or administrative law experience
proposal: The chapter says the SBA Administrator and key staff should have experience in small-business finance and investment or administrative law, not treat the job as symbolic.
quote: the Administrator and his or her key staff should have experience in small-business finance and investment and/or administrative law.

title: Review SBA programs, freeze budget, then cut ineffective ones
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should review SBA loan and grant programs and report to Congress within six months, ranking them by cost-effectiveness. The budget would stay flat until then, after which Congress should end ineffective programs, combine duplicates, or consider cutting the SBA budget.
quote: The next Administration should undertake a comprehensive review of the effectiveness of its various loan and grant programs and provide a report to Congress within six months.

title: Halt SBA lender expansion and outsource where private sector fits
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should stop SBA efforts to expand programs such as more licensed Small Business Lending Companies, properly staff current programs, and outsource work where private-sector expertise is better.
quote: A conservative Administration should rein in these idealistic and impractical efforts, get current programs under control and properly staffed
